Sara: :wave: Heads-up — I'm OOO Friday. Before I hand off can we quickly align on runtime vs SRE oncall boundaries for the rotation? Main questions: degraded model outputs vs infra perf, who gets the initial page, and what to include in the handoff notes.

Mike: Short version — SRE owns infra (hosts, kernels, networking, node flapping, GCE/AZ issues). Runtime owns the model-serving process, autoscaler config, batching/KV cache, and model-level fallbacks. If it's clearly model logic (wrong outputs, hallucinations) runtime. If GPU/host level failures, SRE.

Vinh: Agree with Mike but one nuance: if model is slow because of autoscaler mis-config or batching backlog -> runtime still first responder. If GPUs are repeatedly OOMing or NVML errors -> escalate to SRE immediately. So initial triage should be runtime unless the alert explicitly mentions node/gpu/hypervisor.

Julia: Proposed escalation flow to put in the runbook:
- Pager fires -> primary oncall (runtime or sre depending on alert channel).
- 0-15m: Triage and attempt mitigation (restart pods, switch traffic to fallback model).
- >=15m unresolved: escalate to service owner + secondary oncall.
- If customer-facing SLA breach detected -> page on-call manager + ops lead.
Also add a small severity table to clarify S0..S3.

Mike: On severity defs, suggest: S0 = total outage (all customers blocked), S1 = major degradation (>=50% errors or large latency spike causing user-visible failures), S2 = partial impact (subset of traffic degraded), S3 = non-urgent / informational. Happy to bake numbers into the runbook.

Sara: For the handoff checklist I'll include: current active rollouts, recent perf anomalies (p95/p99), any known flaky models, open PRs touching scaler/autoscaler, and recent infra changes.

Vinh: Add these runtime-specific items: list of fallback models & versions, kv-cache warm status, quantization changes in last 24h. Also include an initial triage snippet to run:
```
# quick triage commands (runtime)
kubectl -n runtime get pods -o wide | grep model-serving
kubectl -n runtime logs <pod> -c model-serving --tail 200
# check KV cache hit rate (internal dashboard)
```
If you see repeated OOM/KERNEL errors, escalate to @Mike (SRE).

Julia: I'll update the runbook with the flow and the severity table, and create a small FAQ for handoffs. Small process rule: when swapping shifts, paste last 6h of p95 + any console errors into the rotation doc/channel so the next person has context.

oncall-bot: Reminder: runbook updated by Julia at 1832110000

Sara: :thumbsup: Thanks all — I'll add the final handoff note to the rotation doc and ping the incoming oncall. If anyone wants to add specific commands or dashboards, drop them here and I'll copy them into the runbook.
